doc.title: Bob Schulz interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Turk Murphy and Earthquake McGoon's
summary: After the war the Watters band split; Turk's club was named from Li'l Abner with Al Capp's permission.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: again. Some of them split and went their separate ways. Turk went his separate way and Bob Scobey went his way, and Clancy Hayes went along with him, and they formed their own little bands. And Turk, I played with Turk, he had a club in San Francisco called Earthquake Magoons, which I think went for about 25 years. And it’s a funny story about it because the name was derived from L’il Abner, so Al Capp was one of the characters in L’il Abner. So Al Capp, they wanted to get permission from Al to use the name. And so they wrote him a letter and it wasn’t long after they got a letter back it says as long as you keep your nose clean and play good music you can have it.
Gee I hope they had that in a frame on a wall somewhere.
